correctness.rationale: At fixed sites the orthogonal L² projection is the conditional mean. The pinned Markov decomposition is piecewise-linear interpolation plus independent zero-endpoint bridges, giving the stated conditional quadratic form. Wick's identity gives Var(Q)=1/45 and explained variance 2 tr((HΣ)^2), including the degenerate designs by the same interpolation with zero-length intervals. Writing r=(y−x)/2 and t=(x+y−1)/2, the centered polynomial has its unique maximum at r=(√41−1)/40 by the derivative sign. For r≤1/4 the polynomial is convex in t²; the extreme off-center candidate has only one effective site and strictly less explained variance. For 1/4≤r<1/2, the derivative in r increases with t² and its upper bound at t²=(1/2−r)² is strictly negative by the reported factorization. Decreasing r to 1/4 at fixed t is feasible and the maximum on that cross-section is strictly below the centered optimum. The pinned endpoint pair supplies no information. Thus the uniqueness claim and the three reported risks are correct.
residual_risks: The symbolic computation corroborates risk identities; the full-triangle comparison comes from the checked analytic proof. No extension to noisy or adaptive observation is implied.
